guarantees.claim: ctr_i_rev is continuously assigned the byte-reversed version of ctr_i.
ctr_o is continuously assigned the byte-reversed version of ctr_o_rev.
ctr_we_o is continuously assigned the sparse-to-vector decoded value of ctr_we_o_rev.

assumptions.claim: ctr_we_o_rev must contain a valid sparse encoding when the AES CTR module is operational.
assumptions.cond: ctr_we_o_rev is read for the ctr_we_o assignment
assumptions.risk: An invalid sparse value could cause ctr_we_o to decode incorrectly, leading to unintended counter write enables and potential corruption of the counter state.

uncertain_points.claim: No local error detection exists for invalid sparse encoding on ctr_we_o_rev; any invalid value passes through the combinational decode and directly affects ctr_we_o.
uncertain_points.cond: ctr_we_o_rev carries an illegal sparse value
uncertain_points.risk: A single-point fault in the sparse encoder or on the wire could cause an erroneous write enable to the CTR counter, potentially breaking the AES crypto stream or causing a data integrity fault.
